newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Chronology of recent events on Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of recent events on Cyprus.

text.p: Greek and Turkish Cypriots have lived apart since Turkey invaded the northern third of the Mediterranean island in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup sponsored by the military junta then ruling Greece.
The United Nations, which has had a peacekeeping force on the island since the outbreak of intercommunal violence in 1964, has failed in its efforts to reunite Cyprus under a federal umbrella.
Following is a chronology of key events from 1994 leading to this week's talks at a resort in New York state between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities:
April 28, 1994 - Months of U.N.-led diplomacy aimed at persuading Greek and Turkish Cypriots to agree on confidence-building measures collapse.
Oct 18 - Greek Cypriot leader Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash start informal consultations in Nicosia in an attempt to breach the deadlock. The talks end without result.
May 21, 1995 - Informal meetings in London between representatives of the two communities to explore the possibility of finding common ground. The talks fail.
June 3, 1996 - Greek Cypriot soldier shot dead in U.N. buffer zone by soldier from Turkish Cypriot side.

Aug 11 - Greek Cypriot demonstrator killed, more than 70 people on both sides hurt when Greek Cypriot motorcyclists defy authorities and push across buffer zone, clashing with Turkish troops and Turkish Cypriot counter-demonstrators.

Aug 14 - Security forces in Turkish-occupied north fire on Greek Cypriot demonstrators in buffer zone in Dherinia, killing a man who tries to pull down Turkish flag. U.N. describes incidents as worst violence since 1974.
Sept 8 - One soldier from Turkish side shot dead, one wounded near buffer zone.
Oct 13 - Turkish Cypriot forces shoot dead a Greek Cypriot man who crossed into the north.

Jan 4, 1997 - Cyprus signs deal with Russia to buy S-300 surface-to-air missile system, prompting criticism from West and threats by Turkey to use military force to block the deployment of the missiles.

Jan 13 - U.S. envoy Carey Cavanaugh sent to island to defuse missile crisis. Cavanaugh says immediate crisis is averted after being told by Greek Cypriots the system would not be deployed for next 16 months.
March 10 - New round of U.N.-led proximity talks starts between two sides in preparation for direct talks.
June 4 - U.S. President Bill Clinton appoints Richard Holbrooke, who mediated Bosnian peace deal, as special emissary for Cyprus.
June 11 - U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan issues invitations to Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders to attend talks in New York state on July 9.
